revised_comments: Namibia operates the Namibia Integrated Employment Information System (NIEIS), a standalone job-seeker and vacancy registry established under the Employment Services Act, 2011, holding over 227,000 registered job seekers as of 2025 and undergoing a further portal upgrade in 2026. Definition: Integration of court records, case management systems, correctional services data, legal aid information
Comments: No evidence found of court records or justice system integration with Nam-X data exchange.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original 0/Unknown score is superseded by fresher evidence. The Namibian (July 2025) and NBC News report that a National Digital Justice Task Force has been established, tasked with defining the strategic vision for an Integrated Electronic Case Management and Information System, with explicit plans to integrate the prosecution, police, correctional service and land registry; the Supreme Court is moving from a paper-based system towards e-Justice, modelled on Uganda's Eccmis. Separately, Allgemeine Zeitung (Sept 2025) confirms the Ministry of Justice has already deployed a case management system for legal aid, with plans to extend it to the Masters of the High Court. This is credible, dated evidence of active development (not yet operational integration), so the score is revised from 0 (Unknown) to 3 (Under development). No source confirms this justice-sector integration is routed through the Nam-X platform specifically, so full/partial integration into the national exchange cannot yet be claimed.
revised_comments: Namibia's justice sector is actively digitising and integrating its systems. A National Digital Justice Task Force, formed in 2025 and chaired by the Chief Justice, is defining the strategic vision for an Integrated Electronic Case Management and Information System with planned links across the prosecution, police, correctional service and land registry, modelled on Uganda's Eccmis. The Supreme Court is transitioning from paper-based records to e-Justice, while the Ministry of Justice has already rolled out a case management system for legal aid administration, with extension to the Masters of the High Court under way.

However, none of the sourced material describes NaTIS being linked to Nam-X or a broader cross-agency data exchange for identity/traffic-offence verification. This is a financial/telecoms-regulator initiative, distinct from the Nam-X interoperability platform itself, and no source links it to data exchange fraud detection, data quality or predictive analytics within Nam-X. Score confirmed at 0 (Unknown/n.a.) for AI within the data exchange specifically; the adjacent AI pilot is noted for awareness but does not meet the variable definition, so is flagged for human review rather than used to change the score.
revised_comments: There is no documented evidence that artificial intelligence is integrated into the Nam-X data exchange for data quality, fraud detection or predictive analytics. A separate, sector-specific AI pilot ('ConsumerConnect') is under way between the Bank of Namibia and the Communications Regulatory Authority of Namibia (CRAN) for citizen complaint and scam-reporting services, with discussion of a shared sovereign-AI infrastructure model across government agencies, but this sits outside the national data exchange platform itself.
